reason:
Completely rewrote HAL_UART_IRQHandler to prevent exceptional loops. The previous implementation had complex logic that could cause recursive calls, especially when calling HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback. The new implementation:
1. Greatly simplifies the interrupt handling logic
2. Removes all hardware register access and flag checking
3. Processes interrupts based solely on UART state (not hardware flags)
4. For transmission: sends all data immediately using HAL_BE_Out
5. For reception: reads data using HAL_BE_In
6. Calls appropriate callbacks based on state
7. Has clear return paths to prevent any loops
8. Never calls HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback from transmission paths
This should completely eliminate the exceptional loop that was occurring when HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback was being called recursively.
